headline: Jab week absorbed; taper vert banked without a descent
narrative: The taper opened with a curveball: Monday's COVID and flu jabs, with an evening club run squeezed in before the side effects arrived. High temperatures followed two nights running, and Tuesday was blank. Wednesday still felt off until later in the day, when an afternoon weights session marked the turn; Thursday's flat morning trail run was the first on-foot session back. Friday added a steep treadmill climb, and the weekend was back to normal — a run out to parkrun and a rare dash of speed on Saturday, weights plus a long treadmill climb on Sunday.

Vert finished a shade over the deload ceiling, which on a recovery week is normally the wrong side to land on — but nearly all of it came from the two steep treadmill blocks on Friday and Sunday, ascent-only machine work that carries far less load than the number suggests. The outdoor runs added only scraps, and deliberately so: not a metre of descending all week, exactly the rest the descent-specific right quad wanted, and no flags of any kind. With Costa Blanca under three weeks out, next week asks for even less — short and snappy, legs springy, and the shrinking target stays a ceiling.
